title: Tangent Slope of a Radical Function via Conjugates
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the slope of the curve f(x) = sqrt(2x + 1) at the point (4, 3) using the limit definition of the slope.

steps.title: Set up the Difference Quotient
steps.explanation: Evaluate the function at 4+h and 4, noting that f(4) = sqrt(9) = 3.
steps.why: Definition of slope as the limit of difference quotient.

steps.title: Multiply Numerator and Denominator by the Conjugate
steps.explanation: Apply the difference of squares identity (a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2 to clear the radical.
steps.why: Conjugate multiplication rationalizes the numerator and exposes the factor h.

steps.title: Cancel the Factor h and Evaluate the Limit
steps.explanation: Cancel h from numerator and denominator and evaluate by direct substitution as h approaches 0.
steps.why: Canceling the common factor h eliminates the 0/0 indeterminate form.
